name: hack-replay
description: Replay your local git history onto a GitHub repository — pick commits from a visual graph, keep their original dates and authors, and schedule each push.

viewsWelcome.contents:
Cue your local commits and broadcast them to a GitHub remote, on your own schedule.

[Open Hack Replay](command:hackReplay.open)

Scheduled pushes only fire while VS Code is running.

hackReplay.maxCommits.description: Maximum number of commits to read from the local history.

enumDescriptions: Keep each commit's original authored date
Stamp each commit with the time it is pushed
hackReplay.defaultCommitDateMode.description: Default timestamp written to GIT_AUTHOR_DATE / GIT_COMMITTER_DATE for replayed commits.

enumDescriptions: Keep each commit's original author name and email
Use your own git identity (git config user.name and user.email)
Use the name and email set below
hackReplay.authorMode.description: Who replayed commits are authored by.

hackReplay.customAuthorName.description: Author name used when Author Mode is "custom".

hackReplay.customAuthorEmail.description: Author email used when Author Mode is "custom". GitHub links commits to accounts by email.

hackReplay.defaultStaggerMinutes.description: Default delay in minutes between queued pushes when using the stagger action.

hackReplay.keepTempOnFailure.description: Keep the isolated temp directory when a replay fails, so it can be inspected.

hackReplay.targetBranch.description: Branch on the target remote to push to. Leave empty to use the remote's default branch (or 'main' for an empty repo).

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Hack Replay runs git commands against the workspace repository, so it requires a trusted workspace.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Hack Replay needs a git repository on disk.
